With only 3% of nodes labeled, the classifier sees very few examples of the smaller classes. Macro-F1 weights every class equally, so poor performance on rare classes drags it down even if overall accuracy or Micro-F1 holds up. DeepWalk's skip-gram embeddings are learned without labels and tend to favor frequently visited, hub-centered structure, so they may not separate minority-label groups cleanly in the embedding space. EdgeCluster instead builds explicit edge-centric community features (clustering-based representations) that align more directly with the group structure behind the labels. That makes its features more discriminative for small classes, which is why it can have higher Macro-F1 despite the smaller amount of labeled data that DeepWalk gets from the same 3% split.
